note: Seed item. Proof that a marketing page can be the product interface rather than a picture of it. The status bar at the foot is the whole trick. Replace this note with your own.

typography.headingCharacter: Monospace at every size including the headline, so the display type sits on the same character grid as the data and a phrase can be highlighted mid-sentence in phosphor green.
typography.bodyCharacter: The same monospace at small sizes throughout, tight leading, with colour rather than weight carrying every distinction between label, value and warning.

composition.structure: A full-bleed terminal window with a title bar and menu row, split into a left marketing column and a right instrument pane holding a flamegraph, a sixteen row symbol table and a log stream, closed by a full-width status bar.

spacing.rhythm: Uniform tight rows with almost no padding anywhere. Density is the argument, and separation is done with a single hairline rule or a change of colour rather than with space.

surfaceTreatment.finish: Completely flat. Panels are distinguished by a one pixel dark rule and a very slightly lifted background, with an inverted phosphor bar at the foot as the only filled surface.

imagery.treatment: The interface is the imagery. A live flamegraph with an amber hot path, a sparkline and a scrolling log stand in for any product photograph, rendered as real interface rather than as a picture of one.

philosophy.text: The design collapses the distance between the marketing page and the tool it is selling by simply making them the same object. There is no screenshot because the page is the screen. Every convention it borrows is from the terminal rather than the web: a title bar, a menu row, a status bar, and colour used as a strict semantic code where amber means hot and green means healthy. Density is not an accident of fitting too much in, it is the claim being made, because the audience reads dense output for a living and would distrust anything airier. The single piece of persuasion, the headline, is set in the same monospace as the data so that even the sales pitch submits to the grid.
